questions.question: What must you keep in your vehicle when transporting chlorine?

options.text: A phone with emergency numbers saved

questions.correctAnswerText: An approved gas mask
questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine must keep an approved gas mask and an emergency kit in their vehicle.

questions.question: Rough acceleration is:

options.text: Not recommended because it can damage the vehicle
Not recommended because it may confuse other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because it can damage the vehicle
questions.explanation: Always accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can harm your vehicle's engine and parts.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Keep your eyes on the road ahead
Look only at the front and right side
Look only at the front and sides
Look at the front, sides, and rear

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the front, sides, and rear
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be aware of everything around your vehicle. Check your mirrors often to see what is on the sides and behind you, not just ahead.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure, what happens?

options.text: The trailer detaches from the truck

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency brakes activate
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes on a combination vehicle. If pressure is lost, the emergency brakes will engage on the trailer.

questions.question: Drivers are usually least alert:
questions.correctAnswerText: Late at night
questions.explanation: Drivers are less alert when driving at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: To prevent liquid surge in tanks, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate slowly
questions.explanation: When driving tanks with liquid cargo, liquid surge can cause control problems. Start, slow down, and stop very smoothly to prevent surge.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, which should you NOT do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use a hook
questions.explanation: Do not use hooks or sharp tools when loading hazardous materials. They can damage containers and cause leaks.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Is a major cause of deadly crashes
Is a good way to reach your destination quickly

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of deadly crashes
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of fatal crashes. Never exceed the speed limit and adjust your speed based on road and weather conditions.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, you should:

options.text: Hope the vehicle works until another driver takes over
Stop and check the vehicle to find the problem

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the vehicle to find the problem
questions.explanation: If you notice anything unusual while driving—strange sounds, smells, or vibrations—stop and inspect your vehicle immediately.

questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tight
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and wear. Each vehicle has specific requirements for belt tightness, so learn what is correct for your vehicle.

questions.question: If a trailer has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) but the tractor does not:

options.text: Do not drive the truck. ABS must be on both the tractor and trailer.
Drive the truck more slowly than usual.
Do not use this tractor. Find a new tractor with ABS.
You can still use the tractor and trailer together.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still use the tractor and trailer together.
questions.explanation: Having anti-lock brakes on only the tractor or only the trailer gives you extra control when braking. You can still drive safely.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is needed to warm up the engine.
Should be done on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly and smoothly. Rough acceleration can harm your vehicle's engine and parts.

questions.question: If you drive a vehicle built before 1998 and are not sure if the trailer has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to turn on the ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes. This will tell you if the trailer has ABS.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are just as likely to roll over as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: The weight of the cargo raises the center of gravity. Fully-loaded rigs are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has:
questions.correctAnswerText: Two air lines.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles have two air lines. One is for service brakes, and one is for emergency brakes.

questions.question: To test the trailer service brakes, you should:

options.text: Drive forward slowly and use the brake pedal to brake.
Back up slowly and use the hand control to brake.
Back up slowly and use the brake pedal to brake.
Drive forward slowly and use the hand control to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive forward slowly and use the hand control to brake.
questions.explanation: First check that air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Then drive forward slowly and use the hand control to apply the brakes. If the trailer brakes work, you will feel them activate.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Is usually aware of what is around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually notices things slower.
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers notice hazards slowly and make poor decisions. Avoid driving near distracted drivers when possible.

questions.question: What can change the height of a vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Heavy loads make a vehicle sit lower. Light loads make it sit higher. A vehicle that fits under a bridge when fully loaded may not fit when empty.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery right after it starts to rain?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Tires are not designed for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first falls, water mixes with oil and grease already on the road. This creates a slick film. As rain continues, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is only a concern if passengers are loading or unloading.
Should never be on the road.
Is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always be careful around stopped buses. Passengers may cross in front of or behind the bus where you cannot see them.
